newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Mostar police shakeup after attack insufficient - U.N.
newsitem.headline: Mostar police shakeup after attack insufficient - U.N.

text.p: The United Nations said on Thursday that the suspension of Croat police officials involved in a shooting attack on Moslems last month in Mostar was insufficient and called for their prosecution.

A U.N. police investigation identified four Croat police officers shooting at a group of Moslem pilgrims trying to visit a cemetery in the Croat-controlled part of Mostar on February 10. One Moslem was killed and 21 were wounded.
A U.N. spokesman said the interior minister of the Herzegovina-Neretva County, which includes divided Mostar, has informed the U.N. of the suspensions on Thursday, but it was not enough.
"We regard this as insufficient. These people were photographed shooting into the backs of fleeing civilians," Liam McDowall said.
"We want to see them subject to the criminal investigation and prosecution," he said.

Croatian media reported on Wednesday that a west Mostar police chief and his deputy were suspended along with two policemen pending a local investigation into their role in the February 10 incident. It said a new police chief was appointed.
All four suspended policemen -- Marko Radic, Ivan Hrkac, Zeljko Planinic and Bozo Peric -- were named in the U.N. report, which also ordered legal proceedings against them.
Michael Steiner, Deputy to the international community's High Representative Carl Bildt, said he would recommend that the named individuals be banned from travelling to Europe and abroad.
Two more officers, Zlatko Pavlovic and Josip Cvitanovic were identified drawing weapons during the shooting and their suspension and criminal prosecution was requested by the U.N. as well.
The U.N. has not been informed about their suspension so far, McDowall said.
